usageNotes: Use this to modify any VM configuration setting — CPU, memory, disk, network, cloud-init, boot order, tags, and more — without recreating the VM. This is the asynchronous variant: it returns a task UPID string (or null if the task completes within `background_delay` seconds), so callers should poll the task status endpoint when a UPID is returned. Many settings (e.g. memory, CPU count) take effect on the next VM start unless hotplug is enabled for that feature; disk and network changes on a running VM require hotplug to be enabled.

examples.summary: Scale up memory and CPU cores on a running VM with hotplug enabled

tips: Use the `delete` param (comma-separated config key names) to unset options rather than sending an empty value — e.g. `delete: 'description,tags'`.
Use the `digest` param (SHA1 from a prior GET) to guard against concurrent modification of the same VM config.
Removing a disk via `delete` moves it to an `unused[n]` entry by default; pass `force: true` only if you want immediate physical deletion.
Cloud-init settings (ciuser, cipassword, ipconfig[n], etc.) require regenerating the cloud-init drive inside the VM for changes to be applied on next boot.
The `revert` param lets you roll back a pending (unsaved) change to a specific key without affecting the rest of the config.

Caller needs at least ONE of the VM.Config.* privileges on /vms/{vmid} — the required privilege depends on which config key is being changed (e.g. VM.Config.Memory for `memory`, VM.Config.Disk for disk params).
